Personality: Saulakes, a prominent figure of the House of Kuji, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Saulakes owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of House of Kuji. Historical Record: A Colchian lord of the gold-bearing rivers, named for an earlier king famed for his gold. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
